# 209 of 213 by-path test loaders are not cache-first, on keys shared by up to 9 files

## Provenance

Measured by AST walk over `tests/` while auditing bug 2bc7 (which repaired three files sharing the
`"mutation"` key). The audit's scope was that key; this is the surface it revealed.

```
total by-path loaders under tests/  : 213
using sys.modules.setdefault        :   0   (the original 9f0b/2bc7 defect is eradicated)
cache-first (name AND __file__)     :   4
```

The four are `test_differ.py`, `test_differ_conflict_resolution.py`,
`REDACTED_TOKEN.py` (2bc7's three) and `test_reconcile_filter.py::_stub_modules`.
2bc7 additionally fixed `test_differ_emits_probe.py` and `test_apply_list_of_mutations.py`.

## The collision surface

`sys.modules` keys registered by more than one test file:

```
outbound_differ   9 files        mutation    6 files
inbound_differ    8 files        reconcile   4 files
differ            5 files        applier     3 files
```

**None** of the loaders for `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `reconcile` or `applier` validates
`__file__`. The original bug surfaced on `mutation` only because that is where a cross-file
`isinstance` assertion happened to exist — the same latent coupling sits on keys with more registrants
and no such assertion to expose it.

## Why this is latent rather than broken

pytest executes module-by-module, so a file that overwrites a shared key is self-consistent while its
own tests run: its module-scoped fixture was built when its registration was current. The failure needs
two things to coincide — a cross-file identity comparison, and an execution order that puts the other
registrant first. 2bc7 was exactly that coincidence, and it presented as a macOS-only `isinstance`
failure on an object that WAS of the asserted class.

## What 2bc7 deliberately did not attempt

A shared helper, so the loader exists once. It is the right fix and it is not mechanical: the
registrants span `diffing/`, `mutate/`, `apply/`, `state/`, `fetch/`, `conflict/` and `orchestrate/`,
and pytest puts only each test's OWN directory on `sys.path`, so a bare-name import does not resolve
across them. Two workable shapes, both with costs:

* a module at the `tests/` root plus the `sys.path` plumbing `tests/_engine_path.py` already
  establishes — works for every caller including module-level constants;
* a conftest FIXTURE — inherited by subdirectories automatically, but cannot serve the call sites that
  load at module scope, and several do.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ONE cache-first by-path loader exists, reachable from every directory under `tests/` that needs
      it, with the `sys.path` mechanism it depends on documented at its definition
- [ ] every loader registering a key that MORE THAN ONE file registers is converted to it — the
      `outbound_differ`, `inbound_differ`, `differ`, `mutation`, `reconcile` and `applier` keys at
      minimum
- [ ] a guard test fails when a new by-path loader registers a SHARED key without validating
      `__file__`, so the count cannot regress silently (the audit above was a one-off scan; a scan
      nobody re-runs is not a guard)
- [ ] loaders that deliberately want an ISOLATED copy keep it, and say so — `test_mutation.py`
      returns an unregistered private copy and `test_differ.py` registers
      `mutation_for_diff_purity` under a distinct name; both are correct and must not be swept into
      the shared helper
- [ ] the full suite passes under a REVERSED collection order for the affected directories, not just
      the default alphabetical one

## Not urgent, and why

Nothing fails today. This is a latent-coupling cleanup whose value is that the next instance fails
locally and deterministically instead of as a platform-specific surprise in CI.

# Addendum: 5-requirement re-evaluation + OSS-validated pattern recommendation

User pinned 5 core requirements: (1) never review a huge diff in one review; (2) accumulate a huge feature off-main, land it all at once; (3) every change reaching main passed LLM review; (4) no invalidation fragility from content-comparison or merge/rebase instability; (5) pattern must be OSS-validated, not novel/Frankenstein. Note (4)+(5) eliminate the prior options: TRIVIAL_REBASE vote-carry IS content comparison; a custom narrowed interaction re-review IS a novel invention; current chain+topic fails (4) (rebases wipe votes).

## Recommendation: Gerrit server-side feature branches + reviewed merge change (the OpenDev-documented pattern)

Stories = small reviewed changes targeting refs/heads/feature/<name>, merged into the branch AS they pass (attestation consumed immediately into branch history — no vote ever needs to survive a rebase; branch history is the durable accumulator, not label state). Feature completion = one --no-ff merge commit of the branch into main, pushed to refs/for/main as its own reviewed "merge change", gated by the same submit requirement, submitted atomically. No rebases anywhere → requirement 4 by construction.

## OSS validation (web-research agent, 2026-07-01, URLs in agent report)
- OpenDev/OpenStack: Infra Manual documents the exact flow (server-side branch via UI; pushMerge ACL; git merge --no-ff + push refs/for/master). LIVE: openstack/swift feature/mpu + feature/threaded active 2025-2026 with story-sized reviewed changes + monthly reviewed master->feature catch-up merges; merge changes carry the standard label gate (change 983874: Verified+2/CR+2/Workflow+1).
- Qt: reviewed merge changes live on codereview.qt-project.org (qt-creator origin/20.0->master merges June 2026); caveat: Qt abandoned ROUTINE cross-branch merges for release maintenance in 2020 (QUIP-16) in favor of cherry-picks — different use case (long-lived release branches) than finite feature branches.
- Wikimedia: ad-hoc merge commits into master confirmed; not documented policy.
- Chromium/AOSP/Go: deliberately linear (chains/topics/CQ) — the alternative school; their objection (merges hide interaction cost, hurt bisect) is the pattern's known weakness, mitigated by CI on the merge change.

## Three corrections vs assumptions
1. Human UI default diff base for merge commits is FIRST_PARENT (whole feature diff), not Auto Merge — auto-merge (conflict-resolutions-only) is a dropdown selection; server default confirmed in Gerrit source (GeneralPreferencesInfo.java). REST default IS auto-merge.
2. BOT TRAP: GET /changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/patch on a merge commit returns HTTP 409 ("Revision has more than 1 parent", GetPatch.java); patch?parent=1 returns the ENTIRE feature diff (violates req 1). No /patch variant gives vs-auto-merge. The bot must branch on parent count and use files/ (no parent param => auto-merge base) + per-file /diff (auto-merge base) + /mergelist. TODAY our voter would 409 -> fail-closed -1 on any merge change (safe failure, but blocks the pattern).
3. Gerrit has a purpose-built changekind MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE ("don't want to trigger CI or human verification again if your target branch moved forward", config-labels.html): add to LLM-Review copyCondition so re-merging after main advances doesn't wipe the vote; a new feature-tip is a REWORK and correctly re-reviews.

## Scorecard (feature-branch pattern): req1 PASS (story diffs small; merge change reviews conflict-delta vs auto-merge; caveat: textually-clean semantic conflicts show EMPTY auto-merge diff — CI on the merge change is the mitigation => open epic smoky-flare-slug/1fa8 Verified vote becomes a required complement, not optional). req2 PASS (feature branches live only in Gerrit; replication pushes main+tags only). req3 PASS (submit requirement has no branch clause — already gates feature branches; every commit reaching main was gated as story change or merge change). req4 PASS (no rebases; votes consumed at story-merge; MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE is Gerrit-native + doc-sanctioned). req5 PASS (OpenDev documented + live; honest caveats recorded).

## RED/BLUE/GREEN replay under the pattern
RED: change A -> feature branch, +1, submit into branch. BLUE: change B likewise (parallel worktrees fine — both target the branch; MERGE_IF_NECESSARY merges siblings without rebase). GREEN: pulls branch (A+B in history), builds C, small review, submit. Merge change to main: usually near-empty auto-merge delta + mergelist + CI. Zero re-review of A/B/C. Zero vote wipes.

## Concrete deltas to implement
a. infra/gerrit/project.config: copyCondition = "changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE"; [submit] explicit mergeContent=true + pin submitType=MERGE_IF_NECESSARY (currently unset/inherited — was already flagged); ACL: Create Reference + Delete Reference on refs/heads/feature/*; Push Merge Commit on refs/for/refs/heads/main + refs/for/refs/heads/feature/*.
b. src/rebar/review_bot/: merge-change code path (detect via revisions/{rev}/commit parents length; assemble review input from files/ + per-file diff vs auto-merge + mergelist; keep fail-closed).
c. keep receive.rejectImplicitMerges compatible (it does NOT block explicit merge commits — config-project-config.html).
d. CONTRIBUTING.md + docs: feature-branch workflow (OpenDev recipe incl. Change-Id amend), branch-lifetime cap, scheduled catch-up merges, branch deletion after merge-back (no Gerrit auto-cleanup exists).
e. smoky-flare-slug (CI Verified vote): elevate to required for merge changes (auto-merge diff cannot catch semantic conflicts).

# Context / Problem

Ticket e39f-5055-f5af-424a makes the reconciler's inbound link-removal path (G5, apply_inbound_records.py::_inbound_unlink_one) converge by removing exactly the mirrored (target, relation) link. The safety analysis surfaced a PRE-EXISTING blind spot inherited from 2b16's design: managed_refs marks a ref managed the instant it is created LOCALLY (reducer/_managed_refs.py — strictly monotonic), so G3 cannot distinguish a brand-new never-pushed local link from a peer-deleted one. G4 (same-pass outbound-ADD suppression) covers that blind spot ONLY when the outbound differ emits the re-ADD; outbound_links.py::_diff_links dedups ADDs direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) ('intentionally NOT deduped on relation'), so a local link whose vendor type collides with an existing remote link in the other direction (blocks vs inward Blocks) is never pushed AND not G4-protected — an inbound removal record for it can reach G5 and remove a never-pushed local link. This is order-dependently true TODAY (when the never-pushed link is the pair's most-recent, pair-scoped unlink removes it after G5's relation match passes); e39f makes the outcome order-independent but does not add a discriminator.

# Approach

Design pass: persist enough peer-link history (e.g. record (relation, target) as 'peer-confirmed' only after an outbound link ADD is successfully applied or the link is observed in a fetched snapshot) so _inbound_unlink_one can decline removals of never-peer-confirmed links. Must reconcile with managed_refs monotonicity and compaction (SNAPSHOT restore).

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a removal record for a REDACTED_TOKEN link is declined and logged
- [ ] a removal for a peer-confirmed link still converges
- [ ] behavior covered by behavioral tests through compute_inbound_mutations/_inbound_update_apply_links

# Explore VCS-derived versioning (hatch-vcs / setuptools-scm) as the single source of version truth

Parked design idea (Option E from the api-stability version-marker analysis). Investigate
adopting **VCS-tag-derived versioning** so the version is computed from the git tag at build
time and is NOT hard-coded anywhere — not in `pyproject.toml`, not in `server.json`, not in
docs. `git tag vX.Y.Z` would become the entire version-bump action, eliminating the
multi-file lockstep bump the release currently performs by hand.

## Context

rebar currently hard-codes the version in `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` and mirrors
it into `server.json` (top-level + `packages[].version`), kept in lockstep manually and
asserted by the release workflow's `authorize` version-lockstep guard. rebar builds with
**Hatchling** and already bakes `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance via `hatch_build.py`. The
mainstream zero-touch pattern is `hatch-vcs` (a thin wrapper over `setuptools-scm`) which
derives `project.version` from the latest git tag.

## Why this is an idea, not ready-to-implement

Several open design questions must be resolved before committing:
- **server.json is not covered.** `hatch-vcs` sets the Python package version, but the MCP
  `server.json` version (top-level + packages) still needs to be produced/synced from the
  same source — how? (generate it at build time, a small sync step, or a check).
- **Interaction with the new release-authorization workflow.** The `authorize` job asserts
  `version_input == pyproject == server.json`. With a VCS-derived version there is no static
  `pyproject.version` to compare — the lockstep guard's contract changes. And the release is
  dispatched-from-`main` with a `version` input BEFORE any tag exists (the tag is created
  post-publish), which is the opposite ordering from tag-derived versioning. Reconcile these.
- **CI must fetch tags** (`fetch-depth: 0` / `fetch-tags: true`) everywhere the version is
  needed, or the version resolves to a dev/`0.0.0` string (a known setuptools-scm failure
  mode). rebar's build-once/test jobs run without full history in places.
- **Interaction with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` baking** and the build-once artifact-identity flow
  (story 6168) must be checked so provenance stamping still works.
- **Blast radius vs. payoff.** This is a large change to fix what is otherwise a small
  lockstep bump; weigh against simply keeping the current manual bump (now that the drift-prone
  docs marker is removed under Option A).

## Acceptance Criteria (for promoting this idea to designed work)

- [ ] A short design note that resolves: how `server.json` versions are produced/synced from
  the VCS-derived version; how the dispatch-from-`main` `version` input + post-publish tag
  ordering reconciles with tag-derived versioning; and the CI `fetch-tags` requirements.
- [ ] A prototype or spike showing `hatch-vcs` deriving `project.version` from a tag without
  breaking the build-once / `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT` provenance flow.
- [ ] A go/no-go recommendation with the tradeoff vs. the status quo (manual lockstep bump).

Discovered from the api-stability version-marker design discussion; sibling of the
version-agnostic-marker change (Option A).

# GitHub Issues sync — provider parity with the Jira reconciler (de-Jira-ify the bridge)

## Context

Discovered from the export/import design brainstorm (`rule-swamp-pupil`, 2026-06-17). We want GitHub Issues sync at parity with the existing Jira sync: bidirectional, incremental, idempotent, dry-run by default.

**Critical design conclusion from that brainstorm:** GitHub sync must ride the EXISTING reconciler framework (binding store + outbound/inbound differs + applier), NOT the one-shot export/import path. Import is stateless / additive / lossy and would have to rebuild the entire binding/diff/conflict/convergence layer to do sync — the wrong substrate. git-bug's bridges confirm sync is bidirectional + incremental, distinct from bulk import. The one thing export/import leaves behind for this epic is the provider-neutral `--strip-external` association notion shipped by `rule-swamp-pupil`.

## What / Scope

The spine of this work is **generalizing the reconciler**, which is hardcoded to Jira in 6+ places:

- `jira_key` in the binding store (`rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`) → a `{provider, external_key}` abstraction.
- `jira-` local-id prefix (`inbound_translate.py:105`).
- ADF (Atlassian Document Format) rich-text codec (`adf.py`) → a GitHub Markdown codec.
- per-type/status/priority maps (`outbound_differ.py`, `inbound_translate.py`) → per-provider registries.
- `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` loop-breaker marker (`inbound_differ.py`).
- `rebar-id:` Jira labels / entity properties used for binding recovery → a GitHub equivalent.

Then add a **GitHub provider**: REST/GraphQL client, auth (token / `gh`), pagination + rate-limit handling, field mapping (state↔status, labels↔tags, assignees, milestone↔?, comments with external-id dedup), and inbound/outbound apply leaves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `{provider, external_key}` binding abstraction replaces hardcoded `jira_key`, with Jira refactored onto it and NO behavior regression (existing Jira reconciler tests stay green).
- GitHub provider does bidirectional incremental sync of issues (create/update/status/comments/labels), idempotent across passes, dry-run default, live writes gated by an env flag mirroring `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC`.
- Conflict resolution + loop-breaker parity with Jira; `session_log` excluded (parity with `EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] reconciler binding/translate/differ/codec layers generalized to a provider abstraction; Jira migrated onto it with no regression (existing tests green)
- [ ] GitHub provider client: auth, pagination, rate-limit handling (read + write)
- [ ] field mapping GH↔rebar (state/labels/assignees/comments/external-id dedup) + Markdown codec
- [ ] bidirectional incremental sync + conflict resolution + loop-breaker; idempotent across passes
- [ ] dry-run default; live writes env-gated; `session_log` excluded
- [ ] tests against recorded GitHub fixtures + integration marker for live

Non-trivial; sized as a standalone epic. Builds on the provider-neutral external-association seam from `rule-swamp-pupil`.

# Idea: self-hosted Renovate on Gerrit — peer-pattern dependency updates through the two gates

Captured 2026-07-09 during the OSS v1.0.0 front-door research (epic breaded-ammonitic-elephant). The APPROVED v1.0 design is Dependabot advisory PRs on the GitHub mirror (github-actions ecosystem only, monthly; PRs are unmergeable notifications the maintainer lands via Gerrit; lockdown bot exempts dependabot[bot]) — see story cardiac-lush-chihuahua. This idea records the researched alternative that would eliminate that departure from the Gerrit-peer pattern, for possible post-1.0 adoption.

## The finding

Renovate (Mend.io — the leading cross-platform dependency bot; what ruff/uv use) has a native self-hosted Gerrit platform (`platform=gerrit`, all Gerrit 3.x): it pushes each dependency bump directly as a **Gerrit Change** — no GitHub PRs — so updates flow through the same `LLM-Review` + `Verified` gates as human changes. That is the Wikimedia-LibraryUpgrader / OpenStack-requirements-bot pattern, off the shelf, and it matches rebar's dogfooding ethos (the dependency bot is just another contributor under the two-vote merge policy).

- Docs: https://example.invalid/redacted and https://example.invalid/redacted
- Mechanics: Gerrit bot account + HTTP credentials; SSH cloning supported (discussion #39625); metadata via a `Renovate-Branch` commit footer (needs Gerrit ≥3.6, satisfied); `autoApprove` exists but would stay OFF (our gates vote); `statusCheckNames` can map Renovate checks (e.g. minimumReleaseAge) onto Gerrit labels.

## Why it was NOT chosen for v1.0 (the blockers to re-evaluate)

1. **Experimental platform status**: Renovate's Gerrit support is officially experimental — maintainers deprioritize Gerrit issues and allow breaking changes in minor releases. Re-evaluate when it is declared stable.
2. **Ops cost**: Renovate is a CLI needing a scheduled runner (cron GitHub Action or the Gerrit host) plus credentials — a new moving part vs zero-ops Dependabot; disproportionate for a monthly, github-actions-only update stream.
3. **`rebar-ticket:` trailer integration**: the Verified gate requires a resolving rebar-ticket trailer on every commit; Renovate has a known open issue with commit trailers via `commitBody` on Gerrit (https://example.invalid/redacted). Adoption needs one of: a working trailer config, a standing "dependency updates" ticket baked into the commit template, or a narrow bot exemption in the require-ticket check.
4. No Dependency Dashboard on Gerrit (built on Issues) — cosmetic at this scale.

## Promotion sketch (if/when picked up)

- Trial on a scratch Gerrit project first: bot account, `platform=gerrit`, github-actions manager only; verify trailer handling end-to-end through both gates; verify the LLM-Review bot behaves sanely on bot-authored changes.
- If adopted: retire the Dependabot advisory-PR flow (delete .github/dependabot.yml or reduce to security-alerts posture), remove the lockdown-bot dependabot exemption, and update the decision records in docs/releasing.md + the dependabot.yml rationale that story cardiac-lush-chihuahua created.
- Revisit triggers: Renovate Gerrit platform declared stable; dependency-update volume growing beyond monthly-actions-only (e.g. a committed uv.lock); the advisory-PR flow proving annoying in practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] (To be designed at promotion — this is a parked idea, not dispatchable work.)

# Proven root cause: a transient GitHub `git fetch` hang becomes a durable `LLM-Review -1` that suppresses its own backfill recovery

## Symptom

`[LLM-Review: BLOCK — coverage-gap (review-error)]` on Gerrit changes 1189 PS1, 1193 PS1,
1208 PS1 (and 4 more in journald since 2026-07-31 — 7 total). Transient: 1189 and 1193
flipped to `+1` on re-review against effectively identical code.

## Proven mechanism (reproduced on the box)

1. Per review, the bot makes a throwaway clone (`voter.py:603` `TemporaryDirectory`,
   `gerrit_client.py:314 clone_change_ref`) whose `origin` is the **GitHub mirror**
   (`gerrit_client.py:359` `remote add origin <tickets_remote>`, then a depth-1 tickets fetch).
2. The attested gate calls `materialize_tickets` -> `resolve_ref(..., blobless=False)` ->
   `_fetch_origin` -> `git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin`
   (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:337-393`).
3. **That fetch intermittently hangs.** REPRODUCED inside `compose-review-bot-1`:
   25 consecutive runs of the exact command, **2 hung past 320s (rc=124)**, the other 23
   finished in **1-3s**. Median 2s; repo is only 80 MB / 54k objects. So this is a hard
   connection stall, NOT a large transfer and NOT load.
4. git has no `http.lowSpeedLimit`/`lowSpeedTime` and no keepalive configured, so the stall
   burns the whole `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` (`repo_snapshot.py:295`) and raises
   `SnapshotFetchError` (`repo_snapshot.py:376-380`).
5. `adapter.code_review_decision`'s blanket `except Exception` (`adapter.py:207-211`) cannot
   tell an *infrastructure* fault from a *review* fault, so it returns
   `_block("review-error", {})` -> the voter POSTs `LLM-Review -1`.
6. **The vote suppresses the designed safety net.** `reconcile.py:205-211` pre-filters on
   `has_llm_review_vote` and `continue`s — the backfill reconciler only re-reviews
   *vote-less* changes. Posting the -1 therefore removes the change from backfill
   permanently, converting a self-healing transient into a mandatory maintainer re-trigger.

Log evidence — every timeout timestamp is EXACTLY the vote timestamp:

    2026-08-01T23:39:03Z  ch1189 PS1   adapter: produce_code_review_verdict raised: git fetch
    2026-08-02T00:22:11Z  ch1193 PS1     from 'origin' timed out after 300s (attested mode
    2026-08-02T04:46:53Z  (4th)          fails closed) ...
    2026-08-02T16:41:48Z  ch1208 PS1

Normal review setup (clone+fetch+materialize) is 14-19s; the failures are a step-function to 300s.

## Alternatives ruled out by evidence

* **"transfer too large"** (the error string's own guess) — REFUTED: 80 MB repo, median 2s.
* **Auto-deploy restarting the bot mid-review** — REFUTED. `compose-review-bot-1` container
  recreation times were 23:25:04, 00:00:22, 03:59:28, 05:37:03 UTC; the four timeouts at
  23:39:03, 00:22:11, 04:46:53, 16:41:48 each fall **strictly inside a single container's
  lifetime** (1208's container `4bd32a5e5170` had been up 12h). A SIGTERM would also not
  emit this log line, and the same container kept reviewing afterwards. The 3-of-4
  "commit landed mid-window" correlation is coincidence — autodeploy fires every 2 min and
  is a sub-second no-op.
* **CPU / credit starvation** — REFUTED: `CPUCreditBalance` flat at ~864.
* **Disk pressure** — REFUTED: root 61% used, /var/gerrit 9%.
* **Diff-dependent** — REFUTED: reproduced with no review running.

## The defect (changeable artifact)

`src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:207-211` converts *any* exception, including a retryable
infrastructure fault, into a vote-bearing BLOCK. The system already has the correct,
tested behaviour for this class one layer up: `app.py:161-176` and `reconcile.py:222-226`
both abandon a hung review **without voting** and let backfill retry — "the change stays
vote-less (fail-closed) and is retried next pass". The two paths are inconsistent, and the
inner `_GIT_TIMEOUT` (300s) always fires before the outer `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1200s,
`review_bot/config.py:30`), so an infra stall is STRUCTURALLY GUARANTEED to take the
vote-bearing path and never the benign one.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A retryable infrastructure failure (at minimum `SnapshotFetchError`, and any transport /
   timeout class raised below the gate) results in **NO `LLM-Review` vote** — the change is
   left genuinely vote-less so `reconcile.py`'s `has_llm_review_vote` pre-filter re-picks it.
   A `VOTER_ERROR` marker is still emitted so `rebar/host:voter_errors` counts it.
2. A genuine review conclusion (a real BLOCK finding, a true INDETERMINATE, a scanner
   abstain, gate-disabled) STILL votes fail-closed exactly as today — no silent-pass hole.
   Nothing provisional is ever posted on the change (that would re-suppress backfill).
3. Degraded-mode safety confirmed: with `RECONCILE_DEGRADED` (events-log unavailable) an
   unvoted change stays unvoted and therefore **unsubmittable** — submit requires the vote,
   so "don't vote" cannot create a pass. A unit test pins this.
4. Unit test: a `SnapshotFetchError` raised from `produce_code_review_verdict` produces

## Discovered while landing bug 9f63

`89d5-61da-b621-47f8` owns the py3.11 CI cell instability, but it is CLOSED, so this preventable defect would otherwise live only as a comment on a closed ticket. Filing it open, because it is a guard we do not have and it cost a landing cycle.

## What happened

A new test in `tests/unit/test_review_bot_in_flight.py` used the idiomatic-looking

```python
with TestClient(app) as client:
    ...
```

to assert ONE field of the `/health` JSON body. Entering `TestClient` as a context manager runs the app **lifespan**, which:

* starts the queue worker,
* starts the **real** `reconcile_loop` (`app.py`) — every other lifespan-entering test in that module stubs it with `_idle_reconcile_loop` (`tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:1462, :1490, :1631`),
* starts the snapshot janitor, whose `startup_sweep` is a genuine filesystem walk (`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:282` -> `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:133 entry_size`),
* and on exit awaits `queue.join()` under `shutdown_drain_seconds()` — a **1200-second** window.

Under coverage tracing on the py3.11 cell that combination wedged an xdist worker. The suite reached 99% and produced no further output until the 60-minute job timeout, three runs in a row.

## Why it was expensive to find

It presents exactly like the runner-side flake it is not. Three of four matrix cells passed; the review-bot test files passed in isolation; the full suite passed on 3.11 *without* `--cov`. Only the complete CI command reproduces it. Attribution needed a controlled A/B:

| tree | py3.11 + coverage + xdist, CI's exact command |
| --- | --- |
| clean `origin/main` @ 1afdbbd0be | 11184 passed, 26 skipped, **16m11s** |
| the branch | **hung at 99%** |

and then `faulthandler` (`timeout -s ABRT`) to see a worker holding a live anyio blocking portal alongside the janitor thread mid-sweep.

## Why a guard is worth it

Nothing in the repo makes any of this visible at the call site. `with TestClient(app)` reads like a normal client construction; the 20-minute drain, the live reconciler and the disk walk are all invisible consequences. The existing convention — stub `reconcile_loop` — is real but undocumented and unenforced, so it is followed by imitation and lost by anyone who writes a fresh test.

## Fix sketch

Cheapest useful version, in rough order of value:

1. A shared fixture (e.g. `review_bot_client`) that enters the lifespan with `reconcile_loop` stubbed, the janitor disabled and `shutdown_drain_seconds` overridden to something test-scaled, so the safe path is also the easy path.
2. A test-lint or `conftest` assertion that fails fast when the review-bot app lifespan is entered without the reconciler stub, naming the fixture to use.
3. Prefer awaiting the handler directly when a test only asserts a response payload — the route returns the dict as-is, so the contract is identical and nothing background starts. (That is what bug 9f63's change ended up doing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test that enters the review-bot app lifespan without stubbing `reconcile_loop` fails fast with a message naming the correct fixture, rather than hanging
- [ ] The shared fixture bounds `shutdown_drain_seconds` to a test-scaled value, proven by a test asserting the teardown completes in seconds
- [ ] The snapshot janitor does not perform a real filesystem sweep under that fixture
- [ ] The convention is stated where a test author will see it, not only inherited by imitation

## Observation

Found while proving the root cause of bug 4bf4 (jscpd live-clone fixture below the token
floor). Not a blocker for 4bf4 — filed so the observation is not lost.

`rebar.metrics.analyzers._jscpd.run_jscpd` reads `statistics.total.{clones,percentage}` and
returns them verbatim. When **no file in the scanned tree clears jscpd's `--min-tokens`
floor (default 50)**, jscpd 5.0.14 returns:

    {"clones": 0, "percentage": 0.0, "sources": 0, "lines": 0, "tokens": 0}

That is byte-identical in the two fields rebar reads to a tree that genuinely has no
duplication. So `rebar metrics` would report "0% duplication" for a tree jscpd never actually
examined.

## Why it may matter

The project already holds the invariant that jscpd failing to answer must surface as
`Unavailable` rather than zero — see
`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::REDACTED_TOKEN`,
and 4bf4's own AC3: "a metric that reads 0 when it means 'I cannot tell' is worse than
`unavailable`". `sources == 0` is arguably that same case, and is currently reported as a
confident zero.

## Why it was NOT fixed under 4bf4

It needs a judgment call rather than a bugfix, and 4bf4's proven root cause was solely the
test fixture. Options:

1. **Treat `sources == 0` as unavailable.** Honest, matches the existing invariant. But it
   turns a legitimately-tiny or empty tree from "0% duplication" into "unavailable", which
   some callers may find noisier. Note `statistics.total.sources` is absent from the minimal
   report shape used by `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup.py::test_parse_statistics_total`,
   so the check must be `.get("sources")` and fire only on an explicit `0`.
2. **Leave as-is.** On any real repository at least one file clears a 50-token floor, so
   `sources > 0` in practice and the ambiguity never materializes.
3. **Surface `sources` alongside the totals** so callers can decide, without changing the
   current availability semantics.

No option is obviously correct without a product view on what the duplication metric should
say about a tree too small to measure. Recommend option 1 or 3 if picked up.

## The defect

`scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` — the deprecated-vocabulary guard wired into `make lint`
— enumerates candidate files with a raw `os.walk` (`iter_repository_files`, ~line 144) filtered
by a hand-maintained `EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES` set (~line 23). That set covers `.git`, the
tool caches, `.venv` and `node_modules`, but NOT `.claude/` or `bridge_state/`.

Both of those are gitignored (`.gitignore:49` and `.gitignore:14`) and both are created by
normal use of this repo: `make worktree` and the agent skills create `.claude/worktrees/<agent>/`,
and the Jira bridge writes `bridge_state/snapshots/*.json`.

## Measured in this checkout 2026-08-06

    make lint  ->  47,312 "deprecated vocabulary" violations
    violating files                       -> 1,393
    of those that are git-tracked         -> 0

Every single violation is in a gitignored path — `.claude/worktrees/<agent>/docs/experiments/...`
(an agent worktree carrying the repo's own frozen experiment corpora) and
`bridge_state/snapshots/*.json`.

## Why it matters

CI never sees this because it does a fresh checkout with no worktrees and no bridge state. But
the pre-commit hook runs `make lint`, so any developer or agent who has ever created a worktree
has a permanently red commit gate for reasons unrelated to their change. The obvious escape is
`git commit --no-verify`, which disables the whole gate — so a hand-maintained exclusion list
that drifts converts a quality gate into pressure to bypass quality gates.

The exclusion list is the root cause, not the two missing entries: it is a denylist over an
open-ended filesystem, so it will drift again the next time the repo grows a gitignored
directory.

## Approach

Derive the candidate file list from git (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`)
so the guard considers exactly the files git would — tracked plus untracked-but-not-ignored —
and `.gitignore` becomes the single source of truth for what is out of scope. Keep the existing
`os.walk` as the fallback for a non-git-repo root (the guard's own tests run it against
throwaway `tmp_path` trees), and keep every existing curated exclusion (`docs/archive`,
`docs/experiments`, the minified `editor.js`, symlinks) applied on top, so behaviour for
tracked files is unchanged.

- [ ] A test proves the gitignored-path case, RED before the fix.

=== HANDOFF #18 ADDENDUM — a CI failure mode worth knowing, and its fix ===

**A change based on an older commit can fail CI on a step whose SCRIPT its tree does not contain — and
it looks nothing like a rebase problem.** 1276 (2b16) took `Verified -1` with:

    python: can't open file '/home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/scripts/check_config_reads.py':
    [Errno 2] No such file or directory
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.

Diagnosis, and the part that misleads: `build-and-test` DID run (so it was NOT the concurrency-group
cancellation trap from #15/#17 — lint + type-check + pip-audit all passed and only the four pytest legs
failed), and there was no failing TEST at all. **CI takes the WORKFLOW from main but the CODE from the
patchset.** `3ad3abe72` ("6754: config-is-read gate for schema fields", change 1257) added
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:434 → python scripts/check_config_reads.py` AND
`scripts/check_config_reads.py` atomically. 1276 was based on `6cdd4b00d9`, which predates it, so the
workflow-from-main invoked a script the patchset tree lacked. Every older-based change in flight hits
this: 1279/1280 were based on `ba3c06ee47` and would have failed identically.

**Fix: REBASE. This is the #17 trap "Rebase-If-Necessary applies at SUBMIT, not to CI" in its most
confusing dress** — the symptom is a missing FILE, so it reads as a broken main rather than a stale base.
All three changes were rebased onto `gerrit/main` and re-pushed; the diff stat was checked against
`gerrit/main` each time to confirm nothing was swept in (4 files / 782 insertions for 1276; 3 files /
750 for the 1279+1280 stack), and `scripts/check_config_reads.py` now runs clean locally.

**A wrong turn I took, recorded so nobody repeats it:** I first checked for the script with
`git cat-file -e <ref>:scripts/check_config_reads.py` inside a `for` loop with `&&`/`||` chaining and got
"MISSING" for EVERY ref including current main — which made it look like main itself was broken for
everyone. That reading was wrong. `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <path>` gave the correct answer
(present on main, absent on both older bases). **Use `ls-tree` for per-ref file existence**, and be
suspicious of a result that says the whole repo is broken.

**The `Missing tree <sha>` push error from #18 is fixable.** 2b16's agent hit it twice pushing a
rebased tree (including with `--no-thin`) and gave up, pushing from the original base — which is what
caused the CI failure above. Running a FULL `git fetch gerrit` (all refs, not `git fetch gerrit main`)
before the push made it succeed first try: the client then has the remote's objects and builds a valid
thin pack. Do that instead of abandoning the rebase.
